race_context: Fayette County School Corporation is the countywide public school district for Fayette County, based in Connersville. State enrollment counts were 3,498 students in 2018-19, 3,103 in 2024-25 and 3,051 in 2025-26 {idoe_enroll}. This guide could not load the district's website, which blocked automated access, and did not confirm the current superintendent from a fetched page.

How members are elected: members run by residence district. State results show District 3 electing two members each cycle (2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024), District 4 one member in 2018 and 2022, and Districts 1 and 2 one member each in 2020 and 2024 {enr_2018}{enr_2020}{enr_2022}{enr_2024}. That adds up to seven seats, but this guide did not find a district page confirming the board's size.

District 3 (2026): the state list shows 'vote for 1', but District 3 has elected two members in every recent cycle, and the two seats filled in 2022 are the ones up this year {in_list}{enr_2022}. In 2022 Chris Hunt (1,364 votes) and Ryan Baker (736) won those seats over six other candidates {enr_2022}. Hunt is running again; Baker is not on the 2026 list {in_list}. With three candidates for what appears to be two seats, this guide could not confirm the vote-for number on the Fayette County ballot.
District 4 (2026): Ann Kirschner, who won the seat unopposed in 2018 and won a three-way race in 2022 (460 votes to 268 and 215), is the only candidate {enr_2018}{enr_2022}{in_list}.

Earlier District 3 races: in 2018 the two seats went to Dennis E. Perkins Jr. (2,622 votes) and Chris Hunt (2,358), who were unopposed; in 2024 Sasha C. Henderson and Dustin T. Munson won the other two District 3 seats in a seven-way race in which Jared M Glaub finished sixth {enr_2018}{enr_2024}.
Enrollment: the district's enrollment has fallen by about 450 students (13%) since 2018-19 {idoe_enroll}.

Technology: in spring 2026 the corporation said it would stop issuing individual devices to kindergarten and first-grade students starting in 2026-27, shifting toward hands-on learning and direct instruction, and that elementary students would not take Chromebooks home over the summer while officials review screen-time practices {k96_tech}.

Budget and referendums: the state's list of November 2026 referendum filings does not include Fayette County School Corporation {dlgf_list}. This guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law SEA 1 affects the district's budget.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of these races.
